# HCard

> The common surface: restrained depth, a readable heading, and generous space for your content.

[Start with the Hearth UI agent index](../../../llms.txt). This reference describes repository source; package.json version: 0.2.0. Match it to the source/release you are using.

## Identity

- Vue export: `HCard` from `@samishal1998/hearth-ui`.
- Custom element: `<hearth-card>`.
- Individual constructor: `HearthCardElement` from `@samishal1998/hearth-ui/elements`.
- Category: Surfaces.
- [Implementation](https://github.com/samishal1998/hearth-ui/blob/main/src/components/HCard.vue).

## Choose and use it correctly

- Use a plain surface for arbitrary content. HAppCard is specifically for an application launcher, HStatCard for a metric.
- The header slot replaces the default title/description header. Default and footer slots hold application content.

## Public API

title, description: string

A `?` marks optional source props. A prop with a default may be omitted even when the source type is required. Internal `formDisabled` and `control-sync` plumbing is excluded below; do not use it in application code.

```ts
type Props = {
    title?: string;
    description?: string;
};
```

### Defaults

No component defaults; omitted optional props are undefined (Vue casts absent boolean props to false unless explicitly defaulted).

### Events

None

Vue-emitted custom-element events expose arguments as `event.detail`, an array. Listen directly on the element. Native DOM events such as `click` keep their normal payloads.

### Slots

header, default, footer

Vue uses `<template #slotName>`; custom elements use `<div slot="slotName">`. Custom elements do not support Vue scoped slots.

### CSS parts

base, header, body

Use `hearth-card::part(part-name)` for an exposed part, or inherited `--h-*` tokens for system-level styling. Native Vue components use the shared stylesheet and `h-*` classes.

## Vue example

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { HCard, HButton } from '@samishal1998/hearth-ui';
import '@samishal1998/hearth-ui/styles.css';

</script>

<template>
  <HCard title="Workspace settings" description="A few thoughtful defaults.">
    <p>Your settings go here.</p>
    <template #footer><HButton variant="primary">Save</HButton></template>
  </HCard>
</template>
```

## Web-component example

Provide a mount point (use a `form` instead of `div` when demonstrating field submission):

```html
<div id="example"></div>
```

The following is bundler-based ESM. For raw HTML, load `dist/themes.css` with a stylesheet link and import `registerElements` from `./dist/elements/index.js` instead. Set array/object properties before connection when they should become reset defaults.

```js
import { registerElements } from '@samishal1998/hearth-ui/elements';
import '@samishal1998/hearth-ui/themes.css';
registerElements();

const mount = document.querySelector('#example');
const element = document.createElement('hearth-card');
Object.assign(element, {
  "title": "Workspace settings",
  "description": "A few thoughtful defaults."
});
element.innerHTML = "<p>Your settings go here.</p>\n<div slot=\"footer\"><hearth-button variant=\"primary\">Save</hearth-button></div>"; // Static example markup only; never inject untrusted HTML.
mount.append(element);
```

## Related components

- [HAppCard](../app-card/llms.txt): A launchable application card with source, status, and optional owner controls. Favorite state belongs to your app.
- [HStatCard](../stat-card/llms.txt): A quiet overview metric with tabular numbers, an icon, and a supporting label.
- [HButtonBar](../button-bar/llms.txt): Group actions without changing native button focus or submission behavior.
